display.purpose: Hero H1 and section H2 titles only; Archivo at wdth 112-118, weight 800.

body.purpose: Running copy, card text, form labels; Archivo at wdth 100, weight 400.

label.purpose: Section eyebrows marked with a small accent square; visually hidden (sr-only) everywhere except the hero locator line.

shadows.name: none
shadows.purpose: Every ateliê-layer surface (cards, buttons, bands, panels) is explicitly shadow-free; --sh-sm/--sh-lg are legacy aliases kept at 'none' for the pre-ateliê block. The sole leftover exception, #cookieBanner (box-shadow: 0 12px 30px rgba(16,16,16,0.12)), is now barely perceptible against the darker Graphite paper it was not tuned for.

motion.name: ease-standard
motion.purpose: The single easing curve (--ease) used for every transition and keyframe animation in the system.

motion.name: startup-choreography
motion.value: riseIn 0.8-1s, titleIn 1.25s, pieceIn 1.1s, routeDraw 1.5s — sequenced 0.15s-1.1s after .hero-go is added to <html>; no grid-draw step remains
motion.purpose: One-time hero entrance fired by the loader finishing: the ice-blue route line draws down from the logo, eyebrow/title/pitch/CTAs/trust list rise in sequence (eyebrow last, 1.1s delay, since it now closes the column), the real work-piece slides in from the right. The previous grid-line draw-in step no longer exists in the codebase.

motion.name: word-reveal
motion.value: wordIn 0.95s var(--ease), per-word delay = 0.28s + var(--i)*75ms (hero) or var(--i)*45ms (section heads)
motion.purpose: Hero H1 and every section H2 are split into per-word <span> elements by JS and rise with a slight 4deg rotation, staggered word by word.

motion.name: plate-wipe-reveal
motion.purpose: Screenshot plates (.tw-mock, .shot-screen), CTA bands, and bundle panels reveal via a directional clip-path wipe on scroll intersection rather than an opacity fade.

motion.name: button-ink-sweep
motion.purpose: Button hover state: a solid color layer slides in from the left to swap the fill color, instead of a background-color transition. Primary sweeps to ink (light); secondary/ghost sweep to the ice-blue accent or ink.

motion.name: marquee-scroll
motion.value: marquee 32s linear infinite, translateX(-50%), pauses on hover
motion.purpose: The full-bleed outlined-type service marquee band. Outline and periodic solid repeats are ink-colored; the bullet dot between words is the pale ice-blue-2 tint, not the primary accent.

motion.name: scroll-linked-zoom
motion.value: animation-timeline: view(), animation-range: exit 0% exit 100%, scale to 1.28 translateY(-4%)
motion.purpose: Progressive Enhancement: on browsers supporting scroll-driven animations, the hero screenshot frame zooms as it exits the viewport; falls back to static on unsupported browsers.

motion.name: cursor-trail
motion.value: requestAnimationFrame lerp, factor 0.22, plus CSS transition on size/opacity 0.2-0.3s
motion.purpose: A small dot (#cursorDot) trails the pointer with easing on fine-pointer devices. Its resting fill is the pale ice-blue-2 tint; it expands and switches to the primary ice-blue accent over interactive elements (a, button, .shot, .tw-card, .faq-q, form fields).

narrative.overview: The build's own header comment still reads "PR STUDIO — ateliê suíço" and the underlying grammar is unchanged: a sheet of paper ruled into a strict typographic grid, exactly one accent ink, and one variable typeface (Archivo) stretched wide and heavy for display, set at normal width for reading. What changed on 2026-09-06 is the world the grammar is drawn on. The owner audited three palette candidates and picked "Graphite Control Room": paper flips from a cream sheet (#F6F5F1) to a blue-graphite near-black (#151B23), ink flips from near-black to a light, near-white tone (#E9EEF3), and the single accent — the previous "Swiss Red" — is now an ice-blue (#3FAEFF) used identically as fill and as text. Alongside the palette swap the owner asked for two structural trims: the hero no longer draws its vertical column rules (no gridDraw animation or grid overlay remains in the codebase), and the "Stalden · Valais · Suíça" locator line now closes the hero column instead of opening it. body { color-scheme: dark } and a #151B23 theme-color meta tag make browser chrome match the graphite ground automatically. There are still no cards with shadows anywhere in the built system; every block is a plane of paper separated by a 1px rule. The one deliberately "unflat" surface is the slate frame (#232D39) that stages real screenshots — though on this dark ground it now reads as a subtly lighter tint of the same graphite family rather than the sharply contrasting navy island it was against cream paper. The homepage's motion grammar itself hasn't changed: a single startup choreography plays once, then scroll-triggered reveals take over — section titles split into words, plates reveal via clip-path wipes, numbers and indices count/jump into position, a giant outlined-type marquee repeats the three services, and a small cursor dot trails the pointer on fine-pointer devices. Everything routes through prefers-reduced-motion and (for the cursor) pointer: coarse.
keyCharacteristics: Paper-and-ink on a dark ground: ink (--ink) is now the light tone and paper (--paper) the dark one — an inversion of the previous light palette's roles, not just a hue swap.

One accent, one pale twin: the single ice-blue accent (--red / --red-ink, identical value) drives every interactive/structural mark; a paler tint of the same hue (--accent-2, #A6E6FF) exists only for two ambient decorative touches, never as UI color.
The hero grid is invisible again: no drawn column rules remain; structure comes only from the single route line and horizontal 1px rules.
One typeface (Archivo variable) still doing two jobs via variation axes: wdth 112-118 + weight 800 for display, wdth 100 + weight 400 for body — unchanged by the palette work.
Real client work (Hotel Alpina, MedVisp) is still staged as "the piece" before any self-description; the About section remains deliberately text-only (no portrait exists).
Motion is still a single startup sequence plus scroll-linked reveals — never idle/looping decoration except the marquee band and the cursor dot.

rules.name: The Two-Ink Rule
rules.body: The entire marketing surface is built from exactly one ink and one accent — plus paper and its rule-line neutrals. The accent's pale twin (--accent-2) is not a second accent; it's a tint of the same hue permitted only for the marquee dot and the cursor trail's resting state. No other hue appears except the structural slate frame and the band panel color, and neither is ever used as an interactive or text color outside its named role.

rules.name: The No-Shadow Rule
rules.body: --sh-sm and --sh-lg are defined for legacy compatibility but the built system sets box-shadow: none on every card, button, band, and panel in the ateliê layer. Depth is never implied by shadow. The one exception, #cookieBanner, still carries a soft shadow inherited from the legacy block, now barely perceptible against the darker Graphite paper it was not tuned for.

rules.name: The Width-Is-Voice Rule
rules.body: Emphasis is expressed by widening and weighting the same face (wdth + weight), never by swapping typefaces, italicizing, or adding a serif/script accent. The .serif utility class exists (legacy name) but resolves to plain accent-colored text in the current world — it carries no serif font.

rules.name: The Dot Rule
rules.body: An accent-colored "." (.dot / h2.display::after) closes the brand mark and every major section headline, tying every H2 visually back to the "PR." logotype.

rules.name: The Ruled-Block Rule
rules.body: Every grouped unit (pillar, step, stat, plan, shot, FAQ item) opens with a top rule instead of a boxed shadow container. Hover states darken the rule to --ink or tint the label with the accent; they never add elevation.

dos: Do keep the palette to exactly one ink and one accent (ice-blue) on paper; reserve the pale accent tint (--accent-2) strictly for the marquee dot and the cursor trail's resting state, and slate strictly for the frame behind real screenshots.
Do express emphasis via the Archivo variable axes (width + weight), never by introducing a second typeface or an italic/serif treatment.
Do close major headings and the wordmark with an accent-colored "." (.dot / h2.display::after).
Do build every grouped block from a 1px top rule, never a shadowed box.
Do use wipe/clip-path transitions instead of opacity-only fades.
Do gate every animation behind prefers-reduced-motion: reduce (and the cursor dot additionally behind pointer: coarse).

Do keep the hero's structure carried by the single route line and horizontal rules only — the grid is a layout scaffold again, not a drawn visual; don't reintroduce a column-rule overlay without the owner asking for it back.
Do treat real client work (Hotel Alpina, MedVisp) as the thing shown first, staged inside the slate frame.
donts: Don't add box-shadow or border-radius to any new marketing component — both are zeroed system-wide by design.

Don't introduce a genuinely new hue. A paler tint of the existing accent is permitted only for the marquee dot and the cursor trail's resting state — it is not a general-purpose second accent. Anything needing a distinct filled-panel treatment belongs in the band role or the slate screen-frame role, not a new color.
Don't reference the legacy --bg/--card/--dark/--line/--ember/--grad variable names in new work — they're compatibility aliases for the pre-ateliê "kept" block, not the current token source of truth.
Don't assume the CSS variable names --red / --red-ink mean the color is red — under the Graphite palette both resolve to ice-blue (#3FAEFF); read the computed value, not the variable name.

Don't fabricate a portrait, landscape photography, or testimonials on this homepage — PRODUCT.md confirms none exist and none should be invented; the About section is deliberately typographic instead of photographic.

Don't treat this system as covering the whole site yet: blog.html, preco-site-suica.html, caso-hotel-alpina.html, and the other legal/article pages (13 pages total) still carry the previous dark-blue design and have not been migrated to this Graphite world.
